text.p: The following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong urges his MPs to guard against undignified conduct.
- Singapore ex-national footballer jailed for criminal breach of trust.
- Sri Lanka Tamil Tiger rebels storm two strategic government military bases.
- Scotts Holdings likely to appoint Yusuf Jumabhoy chairman.
- Telecom players at odds over 'number portability' for handphone and paging users.
- Global strategist of Manila-based stockbroking firm charged by Commercial Affairs Department with advising clients without a licence.
- Hong Kong government will unveil curbs on property speculation next week.
- Ng Teng Fong sells substantial stake in Hong Kong-listed Sino Land Limited.
- Urban Redevelopment Authority rejects Singapore $55.5 million joint bid from City Developments and Republic Hotels & Resorts for Fullerton square as too low.
- Cost Plus, electronic goods chain owned by private company of Jumabhoy family, goes under.
- Singapore International Monetary Exchange's Taiwan stock index futures made debut with 505 contracts traded.
- Goldsmith and fashion retailer Second Chance Enterprises Ltd launches initial public offer of 19 million shares at Singapore $0.30 a piece.
- Malaysia Information Minister Mohamed Rahmat says there's no question of a break-up of monopoly for Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
- Brashs Pty Ltd, Australian home entertainment retailer jointly owned by Japan's Daiichi Corp and singapore's Hotel Properties Ltd, posts four percent higher year-end sales.
- Local resistor maker ASJ Holdings announces it receives stock exchange's nod for listing.
